newsitem.title: UK: Papua New Guinea to restore cocoa crop to 48,000T.
newsitem.headline: Papua New Guinea to restore cocoa crop to 48,000T.

text.p: Papua New Guinea plans to restore its cocoa production to 48,000 tonnes over the next three years after output was disrupted by a volcano eruption and civil unrest, a government official said on Friday.

"We plan to restore the production after a volcano eruption in 1994 and also civil disturbances in key growing areas in earlier years," the official told Reuters at the sidelines of the International Cocoa Organisation (ICCO) meeting.

Papua New Guinea, which saw production drop to 30,000 tonnes in 1995/96 (Oct-Sept) from 48,000 tonnes in the 1988/89 season, has been granted exemption from the ICCO's crop management plan for three years because of low production.

The plan regulates ICCO's output and producers agreed in September to cut world output by a total of 90,000 tonnes over three years starting in 1996/97 to realise a stocks/consumption ratio of 34 percent from around 50 now.

The official, who attended the ICCO meeting, said the Papua New Guinea Cocoa Board planned to make use of the three-year exemption period, starting on September, to restore the production back to 48,000 tonnes.

"We wanted to be exempted because we plan to restore the production by planting more areas and upgrading more plantations. The exemption could be extended, but we have three years now to restore production," he said.
"The board will also use the funding from the ICCO of over a million U.S. dollars to upgrade the plantations," he said without giving other details.
Production hit its lowest level in 1993/94 season with 30,000 tonnes of cocoa produced, he said.
The official said civil unrest related to land problems in the island of Bougainville in 1989 had affected the cocoa farmers in the country's largest producing area.

He said the unrest had since subdued. Bougainville is also the site of the big Panguna copper mine which was abandoned in 1989 by its owners, Anglo-Australian resources group RTZ-CRA, when the unrest broke out.
The official said Papua New Guinea's major market was Singapore in addition to Germany and Malaysia while domestic consumption was still low.
